scope: Only new independent-factor global-budget allocation and wording reviewed. Prior accepted single-matrix derivation consumed directly. No model, data, tensor, numerical test, optimizer, QA score, bootstrap or GPU execution; related-work priority claims not newly re-audited.
mathematical_findings: Independent factors remove the former shared-D coupling; global budget P_fixed+sum((m+n)r) includes all retained coefficients.
The lower bound P_fixed+sum((m+n)k) is necessary and, for the stated independent-matrix equality constraints alone, also sufficient for algebraic feasibility; it is not a quality guarantee.

With fixed Q,Y,T and positive layer weights alpha and equal per-rank cost, selecting largest alpha*sigma^2 marginal gains up to floor(remaining_budget/c) is optimal for this additive proxy; prefix-compatible tie handling is possible.
For unequal per-rank costs, a marginal gain/cost greedy rule has no general global-optimality guarantee.
The allocation optimizes the stated local Frobenius proxy, not full-model responses, AnswerF1 or a trainable update trajectory.
text_clarifications: Explicitly bound q_l by min(m_l,n_l)-k_l or restrict selection to available nonzero residual singular directions; unused budget need not be spent on zero directions.
Specify floor for equal-cost capacity and tie order that respects increasing within-layer singular index.
State explicitly that Q_l,Y_l,T_l and alpha_l are fixed during one allocation; if they change with allocation, the proved ranking optimality no longer follows.
next_valuable_question: Define a bounded-cost, strictly seen-FIT-only Q/Y maintenance rule, including target time and whether/how older constraints are retained when the sketch changes. Determine its declared protected functionality and feasibility/closure criterion under B. No advance proof of F1 is required; an executable falsifiable proxy hypothesis and exit are required.
boundaries: No novelty claim for classical constrained truncation plus marginal spectral allocation.
No automatic model experiment or restoration of factor/PAS/ShortFixed workers.
k=r still allows changes within the old output column space; it does not mean no learning.
A final-factor budget does not bound temporary SVD, statistical memory, optimizer memory or wall time.
